headline: Spend on AI coding
tools went
scenes.sub: from _$0.55B_ — a *7×* jump in one year
scenes.vo: Enterprise spending on AI coding tools just jumped from five hundred fifty million to four billion dollars in a single year.
scenes.caption: AI coding spend jumped 7× in a year

headline: But the data
tells a *different*
story.
scenes.vo: But here is what the data actually shows.
scenes.caption: But what does the data actually show?

headline: Speed is real.
scenes.sub: Yet ~1 in 3 teams~ report productivity ~going down~.
scenes.vo: Speed is real. Yet nearly a third of teams report productivity going down, not up. Faster typing is not faster shipping.
scenes.caption: Faster typing isn’t faster shipping

headline: The efficiency–
throughput *gap*
scenes.vo: The gains often stall at the individual developer. They rarely reach the whole organisation. That is the efficiency throughput gap.
scenes.caption: Individual gains rarely reach the org

headline: Speed brings
~risk.~
scenes.vo: And speed brings risk. AI generated code raises vulnerability rates, leaks secrets, and even invents packages that attackers can exploit.
scenes.caption: More vulnerabilities, secrets & bad packages

headline: get it right.
scenes.sub:
They measure *throughput, security & value* —
not keystrokes.
scenes.vo: Only six percent of organisations get this right. They do not count keystrokes. They measure throughput, security, and value actually delivered.
scenes.caption: Only 6% measure what truly matters

headline: Measure what
*ships*,
not what’s typed.
scenes.vo: Measure what ships, not what is typed.
scenes.caption: Measure what ships — not what’s typed
